# Gevurah — Reader Architecture Boundaries

The Awtsmoos has no boundary, yet every useful keli must guard one line;
Awtsmoos.com lets endless Torah remain usable when each control owns one contract by design.

## Candidate architectures

### A — keep shell CSS and patch selectors
Fast but risks preserving hidden layering and ownership debt.

### B — replace reader controls with a new framework
Powerful but unnecessary; native modules already model preferences, focus, sidebar, command palette, and scrolling.

### C — strengthen the existing reader-control architecture
Preferred. Preserve public IDs and module entrypoints, improve local tokens/styles, and split only files that actually mix responsibilities.

### D — Shadow DOM reader shell
Strong isolation but incompatible with current ID-based contracts and not justified by present evidence.

### E — inline per-control styles
Rejected. Violates localized modular CSS and future maintainability.

## Boundaries for the chosen architecture

- `.post-reader-localized-context` remains the reader style owner.
- Existing control IDs remain stable unless all consumers are proven migrated.
- Preference/storage modules remain separate from DOM gates.
- Typography gate owns typography-surface lifecycle only.
- Sidebar gate owns sidebar visibility only.
- Popover coordination may close competing surfaces but must not become a god-object.
- CSS layering uses reader-local custom properties, not arbitrary numeric escalation across unrelated surfaces.
- Fixed/mobile reader UI respects safe-area insets and never depends on `100vw`.
- Any touched source above 120 lines is split by responsibility, not compressed.

## Files to inspect before final write set

- `styles/reader-controls/critical-shell.css`
- `styles/reader-controls/live-template.css`
- `styles/main.css`
- `logic/listeners/TiferesTypographyGate.js`
- `logic/listeners/SidebarGate.js`
- `logic/listeners/PopoverGate.js`
- `logic/initialization/readerPanels.js`
- `logic/listeners.js`
- relevant reader tests and browser harnesses
